seoTitle: Add a Symbol Watermark to Your TradingView Chart
metaDescription: Learn how to display the stock, forex, or crypto ticker as a background watermark on your TradingView chart and customize its size and opacity.
intro: A pair watermark stamps the symbol you're viewing — a stock ticker, forex pair, or crypto pair — as a large, semi-transparent label sitting behind your candles, so anyone looking at a screenshot or a recording knows instantly what's on screen without hunting for the tiny symbol text in the corner. It lives inside TradingView's Chart settings panel, alongside the rest of your candle and price-scale display options, which is also why it's easy to miss the first time you go looking for it. This guide walks through that settings panel, what's grouped next to the watermark controls, and the display choices worth making before you save it to a template.

steps.heading: Start from a plain chart so you can compare
steps.body: Before turning anything on, it helps to look at your chart in its default state — candles, moving averages, and a watchlist down the side, with nothing marking the symbol except the small text in the top-left legend. Once you enable the watermark you'll see the difference immediately, since it's meant to be visible from across the room, not just readable up close like the legend text is.

image.caption: A standard TradingView chart before any watermark is applied — the only symbol identifier is the small legend text in the top-left corner.

steps.heading: Open Chart settings and find the Symbol tab
steps.body: Click the gear icon in the chart's top toolbar to open Settings, which opens with several tabs down the left side — Symbol, Status line, Scales and lines, Canvas, Trading, Alerts, and Events. The Symbol tab is where the chart's core display options live: candle body, border, and wick colors, whether bars are colored based on the previous close, and data modification settings like price precision and timezone. This is also the tab where TradingView keeps the watermark toggle, grouped with the other choices about how the symbol itself is represented on the chart rather than how indicators or drawings look.

image.caption: The Symbol tab in Chart settings, showing candle color options and data modification controls for precision and timezone.

steps.heading: Turn on the watermark and set its opacity
steps.body: With the watermark enabled, TradingView renders the symbol name as a large, low-opacity label across the plot area, sized and positioned so it sits behind your candles without covering your price action. Keep the opacity low enough that the text reads as a background element rather than something competing with your chart for attention — the whole point is a quick visual reference for screenshots, not a second focal point on the chart itself.

steps.heading: Check how the Scales and lines tab affects the whole layout
steps.body: While you're in Settings, it's worth glancing at the Scales and lines tab too, since watermark visibility and price-scale visibility interact on a busy chart. This tab controls whether the currency and unit are always visible, how price labels avoid overlapping, and whether a countdown to the next bar's close is shown — all display choices that, combined with a watermark, determine how cluttered or clean your final chart looks.

image.caption: The Scales and lines tab, covering price label overlap, the countdown-to-close display, and per-element value visibility.

steps.heading: Confirm it works the same across asset types
steps.body: The watermark isn't tied to a specific market — switching your chart's symbol from a stock to a forex pair, an index, or a crypto pair keeps the same watermark behavior active, just updating the text to match whatever's currently loaded. That consistency is what makes it useful if you're bouncing between charts for a tutorial or a multi-asset watchlist review, since you don't have to re-enable it every time you change symbols.

steps.heading: Save it to a template so it carries over
steps.body: Once you've settled on an opacity and position you're happy with, save the layout as a template rather than relying on TradingView to remember the setting automatically. Templates preserve your full chart setup — colors, indicators, and the watermark together — so opening a new chart and applying the template gets you back to the same branded look in one click instead of reconfiguring settings each time.

steps.heading: Turn it off when you don't need it
steps.body: For your own day-to-day analysis, the watermark can be more distraction than help, so it's worth switching off for active trading and switching back on only when you're capturing a chart for someone else to see. The toggle lives in the same place you turned it on, so disabling it is exactly as quick as enabling it was.

faq.question: What does the pair watermark show?
faq.answer: It displays the stock ticker, forex pair, or crypto symbol as a large, semi-transparent label across the chart's background.

faq.question: Where do I find the watermark setting?
faq.answer: Open Chart settings from the gear icon in the toolbar, then go to the Symbol tab, where it's grouped with the other options for how the chart displays the current symbol.

faq.question: Can I adjust the watermark's opacity?
faq.answer: Yes — keep it low enough that the text reads as background texture rather than competing with your candles for attention.

faq.question: Does the watermark work for all asset types?
faq.answer: Yes, it works the same way across stocks, indices, forex, and crypto charts, updating automatically when you switch symbols.

faq.question: Can I save the watermark setting to my templates?
faq.answer: Yes — save your layout as a template once you're happy with the size, opacity, and position, so new charts pick up the same look automatically.
